expectations.text: Separate download scripts exist for V-Dem and CEPII Gravity
expectations.evidence: Two separate download scripts exist: '01_download_vdem.py' (downloads V-Dem Country-Year dataset from v-dem.net, extracts democracy indices, filters to 1990-2020) and '02_download_cepii_gravity.py' (downloads CEPII Gravity dataset from cepii.fr, extracts trade/distance/gravity variables, filters to 1990-2020). Both contain genuine download, extraction, and processing logic using requests, zipfile, and pandas.

expectations.text: A merge/processing script exists that combines both data sources
expectations.evidence: '03_merge_democracy_trade.py' loads both processed CSVs and merges V-Dem into CEPII Gravity twice (once for origin country, once for destination) via left join on ISO3 code + year. It also creates derived variables (democracy_diff_polyarchy, democracy_avg_polyarchy, both_democratic, etc.) and outputs both a full merged dataset and an analytical subset. The merge logic is substantive and well-documented.

expectations.text: SOURCES.yaml contains at least 2 entries (one per data source)
expectations.evidence: No SOURCES.yaml file exists in the outputs directory. The complete file listing shows: 01_download_vdem.py, 02_download_cepii_gravity.py, 03_merge_democracy_trade.py, generate_sample_data.py, requirements.txt, data_dictionary.csv, and four CSV data files. Source metadata is documented only in the transcript and in script docstrings, not in a dedicated SOURCES.yaml.

expectations.text: DATA_DICTIONARY.md covers variables from both V-Dem and CEPII sources
expectations.evidence: No DATA_DICTIONARY.md file exists. A 'data_dictionary.csv' was created instead, which does cover variables from both V-Dem (e.g., v2x_polyarchy_o/d, v2x_libdem_o/d) and CEPII (e.g., iso3_o/d, tradeflow_baci, distw, contig) plus derived variables. The content is substantive and correct, but the format does not match the expected .md file.

expectations.text: README.md documents the execution order of scripts
expectations.evidence: No README.md file exists in the outputs directory. The transcript mentions the execution order ('Run scripts in order: 01_download_vdem.py -> 02_download_cepii_gravity.py -> 03_merge_democracy_trade.py') in its Notes section, but this information was not captured in a README.md file within the outputs.

expectations.text: requirements.txt lists dependencies for both data sources
expectations.evidence: requirements.txt contains: 'pandas>=1.5.0', 'requests>=2.28.0', 'numpy>=1.23.0'. Both download scripts (V-Dem and CEPII) use pandas and requests; the merge script uses pandas and numpy. All dependencies for all three scripts are covered.

claims.claim: V-Dem dataset covers ~202 countries from 1789 to present
claims.evidence: Cannot verify against real data since HTTP requests were not made; sample data only covers 20 countries. The claim is plausible based on V-Dem documentation but unverifiable from outputs.

claims.claim: CEPII Gravity dataset covers ~200 countries from 1948 to 2019
claims.evidence: Cannot verify against real data. Sample data covers only selected country pairs and 3 years (2000, 2010, 2020). Claim is plausible but unverifiable from outputs.

claims.claim: The merge handles ISO3 code mismatches between datasets (e.g., Palestine: PSG vs PSE)
claims.evidence: 03_merge_democracy_trade.py lines 54-60 contain an iso3_map dictionary that remaps PSG->PSE, SML->SOM, ZZB->ZAN, confirming this capability.

claims.claim: Scripts create a unified trade_flow variable preferring BACI, then Comtrade, then IMF
claims.evidence: 02_download_cepii_gravity.py lines 145-152 iterate through trade columns in order [tradeflow_baci, tradeflow_comtrade_o, tradeflow_comtrade_d, tradeflow_imf_o, tradeflow_imf_d] using fillna, confirming the cascading preference.

claims.claim: Sample V-Dem data has 20 countries x 7 years = 140 rows
claims.evidence: The vdem_democracy_1990_2020.csv file exists (13639 bytes) but would need row counting to verify. The transcript states 140 rows.

claims.claim: The full merged dataset has 73 dyad-year observations
claims.evidence: democracy_trade_merged_full.csv exists (13079 bytes). The transcript claims 73 rows. Not independently verified by row count.

uncertainties: HTTP requests could not be made during execution, so sample/mock data was generated instead of real downloads
CEPII Gravity temporal coverage may not fully extend to 2020
V-Dem download URL may change with new data releases
needs_review: Scripts should be tested with actual internet access to verify download URLs work
Full merged dataset size (2-4 million rows) may require memory optimization
workarounds: Created generate_sample_data.py and hand-crafted sample CSVs since HTTP downloads were not possible

suggestions.assertion: SOURCES.yaml contains at least 2 entries (one per data source)
suggestions.reason: This assertion tests for a specific file format (YAML) that may not be a natural output of the task. The executor documented sources thoroughly in script docstrings and the transcript. Consider also accepting source metadata in alternative structured formats (e.g., within scripts or a JSON file), or make the prompt explicitly require SOURCES.yaml.

suggestions.assertion: DATA_DICTIONARY.md covers variables from both V-Dem and CEPII sources
suggestions.reason: The executor created data_dictionary.csv which contains exactly the right content but in CSV format instead of Markdown. The assertion conflates content (variable documentation) with format (.md). A more discriminating assertion would check that variable documentation exists and covers both sources, regardless of format.

No assertion checks whether the download scripts would actually work when run with internet access. The URLs, extraction logic, and variable selection are critical to real execution. Consider an assertion that verifies the scripts are syntactically valid Python (e.g., can be parsed without import errors).

No assertion checks the quality or correctness of the merge logic, which is arguably the most important part of this task. An assertion like 'The merge script joins on ISO3 + year for both origin and destination countries' would test genuine understanding of the dyad-year merge challenge.

eval_feedback.overall: Three of six assertions test for specific filenames (SOURCES.yaml, DATA_DICTIONARY.md, README.md) rather than the substantive content of the data collection pipeline. The executor produced high-quality scripts and documentation but in different file formats than expected. The assertions that do pass reflect genuine work. Consider rebalancing assertions toward testing pipeline logic and data quality rather than specific file naming conventions.
